function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** (in this context) refers to an official authorization or instruction given to someone—typically a financial institution—to act on behalf of another party. In banking and finance it usually means: | Aspect | Explanation | |--------|-------------| | **Who gives it?** | A customer (or “client”) authorizes a bank or payment service provider. | | **To whom does it apply?** | It can be directed at a specific person within the bank (e.g., a teller), a department, or even the entire organization. | | **Purpose** | To allow the authorized entity to perform certain actions such as transferring funds, making payments, managing accounts, etc. | | **Scope & Limits** | Mandates often specify limits – e.g., maximum amount per transaction, total annual volume, types of transactions allowed, time period during which the mandate is valid. | | **Types** | • *Standing orders* (recurring transfers)
• *Direct debits* (automatic withdrawals from a customer's account)
• *Payment instructions* (one‑off transfer requests)
• *Authorization for third parties* (allowing a vendor to collect money). | In practice, when you set up a standing order or direct debit, you're creating a mandate that tells your bank: “I authorize you to take/transfer X amount from my account under Y conditions.” Once the mandate is signed and recorded, the bank has legal authority to carry out those operations without needing further approval each time. If you’re dealing with APIs like `partner_mandates` or `user_mandates`, they let software systems query or manage these authorizations programmatically—for example, retrieving all pending mandates for a particular user or listing all active mandates issued by a partner.
